subject: Acme - Post-call recap: deployment mode tradeoffs (latency vs throughput)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 15:07:00 -0800
Subject: Acme discovery recap — latency/throughput gating the deployment mode

Thanks for joining the call earlier. Quick internal recap and asks so we can align next steps with Acme (Susan). High-level: they have a customer-facing product that will call an LLM for short-form completions (avg prompt+completion ~120 tokens). Key constraints they repeatedly mentioned: 99th pct latency target ~<150ms for single-token streaming responsiveness for micro-interactions, and burst QPS up to ~600 req/s during peak campaigns.

What we heard:
- Preferred path: Hosted API for speed to market and simpler billing.
- Concern: ability to guarantee tail latency and burst throughput under promo-driven surges.
- Data residency: must remain in US only (ok for our hosted region).
- Security: standard SOC2 + contract-level logging/retention acceptable; no air-gapped needs today.

My initial read: if they truly need 99p <150ms at 600 peak QPS, we should evaluate Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) for predictable SLOs. However, we can propose a staged approach: Host them on Hosted API with a Dedicated reserve (burst reservation / capacity reservation) or an SLA add-on and run an early latency stress test (synthetic workload) to validate tail behavior before they commit to Dedicated.

Next internal asks:
1) Dev — can you outline what the Hosted + burst reservation profile would look like (instance types, estimated sustained vs burst throughput, expected 95/99 latencies for a 13B FP16 quantized model)?
2) Marissa — can you draft two commercial paths: (A) Hosted + reserved burst (monthly min + burst billing) and (B) Dedicated baseline with autoscaling and fallback to hosted? Include rough first-year TCO.

I attached their MRQ (acme-mrf-reqs.xlsx) and our Dedicated one-pager I promised. I also put a tentative POC plan in Drive. Planning to send a short note to Susan with a checklist of clarifying questions and propose a latency test window next week.

Karthik
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme discovery recap — latency/throughput gating the deployment mode

+1 on the staged approach. Some technical notes from the call and my quick back-of-envelope:

- Workload shape: short prompts (~40 tokens) + short completions (~80 tokens) is friendly for kv-cache and continuous batching. However, achieving 99p <150ms at 600 QPS requires careful batching policy and a low-seq-penalty kernel.
- If they use a 7B-13B family model quantized (4-bit), we can likely hit 95p <120ms on a 4090-ish instance at moderate batching (batch windows tuned to 10-20ms). 99p is tougher — depends on request batching variance.
- Dedicated gives us control (consistent batching, pinned kernels, reserved GPU count) so tail SLOs are far more reliable. Hosted with burst reservation is viable if we reserve enough GPUs and enable deterministic routing to reserved capacity during campaign windows.

Questions for Acme (to include in your note):
- Precise concurrency distribution (do they expect sustained 600 QPS or short spikes of 20-30s?)
- Average and 95/99 token lengths for real requests (not marketing estimate)
- Are they okay with a short warm-up (30-60s) for KV cache if cold start impacts tail latency?

I'll draft a simple latency test harness (k6 + synthetic prompt set) and estimate the GPU-hours for a 2-day stress run. If they want guaranteed 99p, we should map to a Dedicated SKU and include an SLO/governance clause.

—Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Park <susan@acme.io>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick follow-up + clarifying questions + proposed latency test window

Hi Susan — great to meet earlier. Short follow-up with options and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a tight POC and, if helpful, a one-page commercial.

Summary of options (tradeoffs):
A) Hosted API (fastest to ship): Redwood-hosted model endpoints in US region. Pros: immediate onboarding, simple per-token pricing. Cons: tail latency depends on load; for predictable 99p behavior at very high QPS we recommend pairing with a reserved burst allocation.
B) Dedicated (reserved capacity): GPU pool dedicated to Acme workloads. Pros: predictable tail latency and throughput headroom, easier to hit 99p SLOs. Cons: higher monthly commitment; longer lead time for capacity provisioning.

Clarifying questions to scope correctly:
1) During peak promos, do you expect sustained 600 req/s for >5 minutes, or short bursts (tens of seconds)?
2) Can you share a sample of real request sizes (prompt + completion token distribution) for a representative day?
3) Are there hard contractual SLA needs around 99th percentile latency (i.e., an explicit number that must be guaranteed)?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Option 1: 48-hour latency and burst test (we can run a synthetic load from our US region) — proposed window Tue/Wed next week. Dev will own the test harness; we'll need a sample traffic file from you.
- Option 2: If you prefer, we can draft a Dedicated baseline quote (monthly reserve + autoscale policies) — Marissa will send a commercial path A/B.

Attachments: acme-mrf-reqs.xlsx (you shared), redwood-dedicated-one-pager.pdf

Would you prefer we run the test first or send the two-path quote? Either works from our side.

Cheers,
Karthik
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
From: Susan Park <susan@acme.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + clarifying questions + proposed latency test window

Thanks, Karthik — this is helpful. Short answers below:

1) Bursts: typically short but intense — most bursts 30–90s; during larger campaigns we can see sustained ~5 minutes but not frequently.
2) Attached a CSV with sampled request stats (see also the MRQ). Typical prompt length 35–60 tokens; completions 60–120 tokens.
3) SLA: our product team would like to see 99p under 200ms ideally; negotiable if we get strong compensating guarantees on availability and cost predictability.

Plan: we prefer Hosted first for time-to-market but need a clear path to Dedicated if the test shows we can't meet tail latency. Please send the test plan and a short cost comparison. Procurement looped here — they will need the quote if we move to Dedicated.

—Susan
Director of Product | Acme Corporation

Great — Susan's preference for Hosted-first with a defined escalation to Dedicated if the 48-hour test misses the 99p target gives us a clear path. Action items: 

- Dev: please share the test harness + GPU-hour estimate by EOD Monday so I can lock the Tue/Wed window. Include the expected 95/99 output for the 13B quantized profile and configuration we discussed.
- Marissa: please prepare a 2-path quote (Hosted + reserved-burst path; Dedicated baseline with monthly reserve and expected autoscale costs) and a short note on contractual SLA language we can offer for the Hosted-burst case. Procurement will need this to review.
- Me: I'll gather the sample CSV Susan attached and confirm the test window when Dev posts the harness. I'll also prep a short internal risk note for CS (onboarding/rollback steps) in case tail latency necessitates fast Dedicated provisioning.

I'll mark this as priority. If we can get the harness and the quote by Monday, we can run the 48-hour test on Tue/Wed and have initial telemetry by Thu.
